newsitem.title: EGYPT: Africa stock exchanges plan joint sales pitch.
newsitem.headline: Africa stock exchanges plan joint sales pitch.

text.p: African stock exchanges, the minnows of world share trading, pledged on Wednesday to work together to increase their share of foreign investment funds.

Members of the African Stock Exchange Association (ASEA) agreed to set common standards for listings, for education in financial markets, and, where possible, for clearance and settlement of share deals.
They also plan to advertise their wares on the Internet.

Newly-appointed ASEA chairman, Hayford Alile of the Nigeria stock exchange, said at the end of the association's annual meeting:"We hope to set minimum listing requirements across Africa. If exchanges have shared listing standards there won't be any problems in multiple listings."

That would allow companies much more scope for listing on more than one exchange, removing one of the biggest barriers to foreign portfolio investment in Africa -- the lack of liquidity on any one exchange.

Alile, chief executive of the Lagos exchange, said the association agreed to work together to sell Africa as a single investment prospect for the rest of the world. ASEA members will combine to tell their story at the world conference on emerging markets in Cancun, Mexico, next April.
The member countries will also advertise their exchanges on the Johannesburg stock exchange's Internet site, as a preliminary step to developing their own sites.
Outgoing chairman, Roy Andersen, said members agreed to share information on trading surveillance and on release of company results and news.
Andersen, executive president of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, said ASEA members agreed to exchange information on standards for clearance and settlement of share deals.

Discussing the aim to set common listing requirements he said, "Harmonisation will not only facilitate dual listings in Africa but will also make it easier for foreign investors to understand the requirements of each of the markets."
